decisions.reason: "raged like a storm" keeps the 폭풍 image while being more dynamic than "was like a storm."
BASE order reads naturally; SOL's front-loaded modifier with postponed verb ("...to follow collided") is heavy.
"twisted aside" naturalizes 몸을 뒤집었다; smoother than "flipped his body / grazed past."
"as though they were one" is tighter for 한 몸처럼.
"only for the First Elder to" more idiomatic than "only to have ... cut him off."
"shot upward" cleaner than "surged straight up."
Drops the awkward article before mass-noun "Pale Sword Energy"; "One strike" fine for 일도양단.
SOL adds "emerged" (leaving the cloud), an action the source does not give; BASE faithful and readable.
"since childhood" concise and "opponent was ... formidable" captures 상대가 좋지 않았다.
SOL preserves 온몸으로 (bodily involvement), which BASE omits.
"damned old bastard" is the natural adjectival form.
"chuckled" is economical and conveys the 허허 laugh.
Synonymous "appeared/looked" substitution with no real gain.
"Numbers mattered even in..." / "How much more so..." reads with better rhythm than BASE.
"overrate/overestimate" is a synonym swap, no gain.
BASE is direct; SOL's "the aging of his body" is the abstract noun-heavy phrasing the brief warns against.
SOL adds "smile" not present in 씁쓸히 자조한.
"even fiercer" vs "fiercer still" is a synonym swap, no gain.
"give ground" is idiomatic for 밀리다 and the sentence flows better.
"limbs" naturalizes 손발 cleanly; "minor wounds" fine for 잔 상처.
안색 is complexion/face; BASE is closer and there is no real gain.
SOL's structure with "bearing down" reads more smoothly than BASE's "had been driving in."
"in/amid a spray of blood" is an even swap, no gain.
"confirmed his face" is an awkward collocation; SOL's "saw his face" is natural and the recognition is clear from the tongue-click.
"give out" is idiomatic for a voice about to break.
Article before the title is standard English; SOL's change yields no gain.
"not particularly advanced" is more natural than BASE's "not high."
BASE keeps 쏟아졌다 "poured"; SOL's "blazed in" changes the image.
"set the hearts ... ablaze" fine, and "the Jin Family's" shorthand is already used elsewhere in the baseline.
BASE keeps the coupling of a Peak master's prowess with a dog's death; SOL splits it into two separate fears.
"briefly forgotten" matches 잠시 잊고 있던 better than "set aside."
The comma adds a deliberate beat; dropping it yields no gain.
"traitors" fits the betrayal/배신 framing of 역도.
제일 modifies 먼저 ("first"); SOL's "most ashamed" shifts the superlative onto the shame.
Comma-splice join yields no real improvement.
BASE's "another life went out" is more vivid; SOL nominalizes into "Each flash ... extinguished."
"stiffened" is tighter than "had gone stiff."
"surged in from every direction" reads naturally for 몰려들었다.
SOL's "their martial arts" is ambiguous with "the Elders" as nearest antecedent; BASE's "opponents'" is clear.
"seized the opening" is natural; "amid that distraction" fits 그사이.
BASE's "Before he knew it" matches 부지불식간에 and keeps "surged up."
"faltered" and "by his side" read more smoothly.
"from head to toe" is idiomatic for 전신.
"burrow" matches 파고들다 more closely than "drive."
"ran wild/rampaged" is an even swap, no gain.
Even swap of "went/turned" and "Soon/A moment later," no gain.
BASE keeps the progressive 목이 떨어지고 있었다 ("was falling"); otherwise no gain.
"took up the cry" shifts 잇따라 외쳤다 (shouted in succession); BASE accurate.
"traitors" consistent with the betrayal theme and H033.
"invigorated" is concise and natural.
"With their leadership all but annihilated" is tighter for 수뇌부가 괴멸하다시피 한.
"Enough of that nonsense" is natural spoken dialogue for 멍청한 소리 작작 하게.
"commanders' orders" avoids BASE's redundant "command's orders."
Adding "their" and reordering yields no gain.
SOL keeps the imperative "wipe them all out"; BASE converts the order into first-person "we'll wipe."
BASE's cleft matches the topicalized 밀리는 것은 … 흑의인들이었다.
"exploiting every opening" is clearer than BASE's self-contradicting "wasting no opening."
BASE's "Don't fall back! ... dies!" is a punchier barked order; SOL's "Do not retreat" is stiffer.
"silently swung his sword" is more concise for 묵묵히.
"his eyes ... his hands reached toward" keeps the source's body-part parallelism; no gain otherwise.
SOL avoids using the rank term "Elder" for the vocative 어르신; "had lost count" natural for 모르겠다.
Even swap of "at the point of a sword/swordpoint"; no gain.
SOL adds "At last" and "fierce," neither in the source; BASE's cleft matches 막아선 것은 … 사내였다.
"seize" is closer to 장악 than "take."
"a hint of" vs "a moment's" is an even swap, no gain.
"Everyone except one"/reordering yields no gain.
Reordering and "tell me/answer" are an even swap, no gain.
"low voice" matches 나직한; BASE's "quiet" is off.
"chances/opportunities" is an even swap, no gain.
Korean uses uniform present 없디/마찬가지지; SOL's split into "did ... do" adds an unsupported tense shift.
BASE's "leapt from" matches 튀었다; SOL's "flared in" changes the motion.
BASE keeps the specific image 찌꺼기 ("dregs"); SOL's "remnant" is generic.
"someone somewhere beyond him" is tighter for 어딘가에 있을 한 사람.
"last key" vs "final key" is an even swap, no gain.
BASE preserves 글쎄 ("Well?") and the 여유 부리다 sense of "take it easy."
"froze/went rigid" is an even swap, no gain.
BASE preserves the idiom 눈에 넣어도 아프지 않을 ("apple of his eye"); SOL flattens it to "precious."
SOL matches 잠시 잊고 있던 with "briefly slipped his mind"; BASE's "let slip" misreads it.
BASE keeps 서릿발 같은 음성 ("voice like frost") and 터져 나왔다; SOL adds "command," which the source does not say.
"Take care of" is natural for 맡아라; BASE's bare "Take the First Elder" is stiff.
십여 is about ten; SOL's "a dozen or so" overstates the count.
"open a path" is consistent with the same shout rendered that way elsewhere in the chapter.
SOL adds "back" (not in 문득 바라보았다); BASE is faithful with no prose defect.
"line/sentence" for 한마디 is an even swap, no gain.
"authority vested in me as" reads with the correct official register for the formal decree.
BASE's "for the battlefield" matches 전장을 향해; SOL's "across" shifts the direction.
"turned against them" clarifies 전세가 기운 지 오래.
"gets in/stands in his way" is an even swap, no gain.
Restructuring yields no gain over BASE's clean two-beat form.
"bring himself to" matches 차마 "could not bear to" better than "let himself."
BASE's "chest clutched in his arms" is awkward and SOL omits the 끌어안고 action entirely; this keeps the clutching and reads naturally.
decisions.replacement: How long had he run, clutching his pounding heart? When he finally reached his destination, his eyes flew wide.

decisions.reason: SOL's "in the world" adds emphasis beyond 이게 무슨; no gain.
BASE keeps 충격 그 자체 ("shock itself"); SOL's "utterly shocking" is generic.
Rewording yields no gain over BASE's faithful phrasing.
"after/when" is an even swap, no gain.
BASE keeps 실전 ("real battles"); SOL drops "real."
"hits/attacks" is an even swap, no gain.
BASE's "proper Hunter" matches 정식; SOL adds "licensed," an unsupported specificity.
"a living hell" vs "really was hell" is an even swap, no gain.
"come up with the right ... response" fixes BASE's strained collocation "pull the right position."
BASE's "And right now" is literal for 그리고 지금; SOL's "And yet" adds contrast not in the source.
"Keep throwing!" is more concise; object is implied in 계속 뿌려.
BASE's "wasn't worth shit" keeps the crude US register of 쥐뿔도 쓸모없다; "fuck-all" is anglicized.
Article addition yields no gain over the clipped 탱커? 힐러?
BASE's "fucking moron" preserves the strength of 병신; SOL softens it to "the idiot."
